newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African millers, unions see end to sugar strike.
newsitem.headline: S.African millers, unions see end to sugar strike.

text.p: Thousands of striking sugar industry workers, who have closed 14 South African mills and refineries for 10 days, could be back at work late next week, officials said on Friday.
About 4,000 workers embarked on a wage strike on July 2 to demand a 20 percent salary increase from Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd. The companies offered 10.5 percent.

"If we get positive feedback from our guys over the weekend to the latest proposals, and a positive response from the employers in negotiations early next week, we could be back at work by Wednesday or Thursday," union spokesman Eric Botha said.

Botha said the major outstanding issue was the question of backpay in the latest proposal. Employers have offered an 11.5 percent increase backdated to June 1, with an additional increase of two percent in October.
The five unions representing the workers want the agreement to be backdated to April 1, Botha said.
"We (the union negotiators) have gone way beyond our mandate which was 15 percent, but in the interests of everybody concerned we took the initiative to go to 11.5 percent."
The workers would give their feedback on the deal over the weekend, he added.
A spokesman for the sugar companies said the strike could be resolved next week.
"We will just have to see what happens at negotiations next week. I am cautiously optimistic that it will be over next week," said Bheki Sibiya.
He said the crushing season which normally runs from April to early December, could be extended to make up for production lost in the strike.
An estimated production of 83,500 tonnes of cane per day is being lost, but the industry has declined to put a value on the figure.
